category: Solver Diagnostics, Examples and Workflow Reference
description: Numbered ERROR/WARNING/NOTE messages of the Feko 2026.1 solver, PREFEKO, RUNFEKO, OPTFEKO and the adaptive-sampling component with causes and fixes, CADFEKO geometry faults and repair tools, the Example Guide by chapter, the CADFEKO ribbon, command-line diagnostic utilities and the 2025-2026.1 release highlights.

tools.name: Feko message types and where messages appear (ERROR, WARNING, NOTE)
tools.description: Feko reports numbered messages of three types: an ERROR is fatal and must be fixed before the simulation or process can continue, a WARNING flags a condition that might give inaccurate results or a setting that is not allowed or was disabled, and a NOTE gives potentially useful information. The 2026.1 Errors, Warnings and Notes Reference lists the messages per component (FEKO solver, PREFEKO, RUNFEKO, OPTFEKO, ADAPTFEKO) with the message text as the cause, plus a separate list of CADFEKO geometry faults. Look the number up in that reference, then correct the model.
tools.usage: .out file (search for ERROR / WARNING / NOTE); 'Executing prefeko', 'Executing optfeko' and 'Executing runfeko' dialogs when launched from a GUI (messages grouped by type on tabs); CADFEKO 'Importing file' dialog for geometry faults; terminal output when a component runs from the command line.

parameters.name: ERROR nnnn
parameters.description: Fatal; the solver or utility stops. Some solver entries are listed as 'Error Signal' (process terminated by Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Break, kill or a licence error).

parameters.name: WARNING nnnn
parameters.description: The run continues; results may be inaccurate or a setting was ignored.

parameters.name: NOTE nnnn
parameters.description: Information only, e.g. NOTE 35179 (GPU found) or NOTE 48414 (memory estimate).

parameters.name: Error, Note or Warning nnnn
parameters.description: Reference heading for numbers whose severity depends on context, e.g. 36002 (iterative solution diverges) or 39442 (badly oriented cable segments).

tools.example:
findstr /n /c:"ERROR" /c:"WARNING" /c:"NOTE" model.out

Console form (runfeko on a missing model, 2026.1):
ERROR  20006:
File "x.pre" or "x.fek" not found (possibly also no "x.cfx" available)
tools.notes: Definitions and message locations verified in the installed 2026.1 reference (How to Interpret Messages). When a message names a mesh element number, locate it in POSTFEKO: 3D View contextual tab set > Mesh tab > Tools group > Find Elements (element type plus comma-separated IDs) - verified in the POSTFEKO user guide. The reference gives only the message text (the cause); fix steps in this category come from the cited how-to pages or standard practice.

tools.name: ERROR 20006 (RUNFEKO): model file not found
tools.description: RUNFEKO could not find the input: it looks for <name>.pre or <name>.fek and, if neither exists, for <name>.cfx to generate them. Typical causes are a typo in the model name, running in the wrong working directory, or passing an option such as --version or --help as the first argument, which RUNFEKO takes as the file name. Related RUNFEKO file errors are 20022 (file not found when --execute-prefeko forces PREFEKO), 20036 (file needed to execute PREFEKO for a time/date dependency or remote launch not found) and 20067 (file not found when --execute-cadfeko_batch forces CADFEKO_BATCH).
tools.usage: runfeko FILENAME [OPTIONS]   (FILENAME first; base name or .cfx/.pre/.fek; run in the model folder)

parameters.name: FILENAME
parameters.description: Base name of the model; must be the first argument.

parameters.name: --execute-prefeko / --execute-cadfeko_batch
parameters.description: Force regeneration of .fek / .cfm; the source .pre / .cfx must exist, otherwise ERROR 20022 / 20067.

tools.example:
C:\work> runfeko dipol
ERROR  20006:
File "dipol.pre" or "dipol.fek" not found (possibly also no "dipol.cfx" available)
Fix: cd to the folder that holds dipole.cfx and run: runfeko dipole
tools.notes: Message text and console layout verified by running runfeko 2026.1 (also reproduced through runmgrfeko with a dummy model list). 'runfeko --version' fails the same way; the banner printed by every runfeko call already shows the version. Bare 'runfeko' prints banner and usage with exit code 2.

tools.name: RUNFEKO launch-option and MPI errors (20002-20088)
tools.description: RUNFEKO validates its command line and parallel environment before starting PREFEKO or the solver. Option errors: 20002 too many arguments, 20003/20137 no number after -np, 20004/20136 invalid process count, 20005 unknown option, 20012 no file name after --machines-file, 20026/20027 missing or invalid --priority, 20031 no host after --remote-host, 20069 --use-openmp-threading without -np, and 20088 optimisation combined with continuous frequency data (use discrete sampling). MPI-environment errors: 20020 FEKO_MPI_ROOT not set, 20045 invalid FEKO_WHICH_MPI, 20053 FEKO_WHICH_MPI not defined, 20052 MPI does not support Windows CCS/HPCS, 20087 mpiexec.exe for MS-MPI not found.
tools.usage: runfeko FILENAME [-np x] [--machines-file m] [--priority p] [--remote-host h] [--use-job-scheduler] [--use-openmp-threading] ...

parameters.name: -np x
parameters.description: Needs a valid integer (ERROR 20003/20004); ignored with --use-job-scheduler (WARNING 20050/20133).

parameters.name: --machines-file m
parameters.description: Needs a file name (ERROR 20012); ignored with --use-job-scheduler (WARNING 20049).

parameters.name: FEKO_MPI_ROOT / FEKO_WHICH_MPI
parameters.description: Set by the installation; inspect with 'envfeko --plain' (ERROR 20020/20045/20053).

parameters.name: NOTE 31127
parameters.description: OpenMP threading ignored because performance is better without it.

parameters.name: WARNING 20035
parameters.description: Killing a remote job may leave Feko files on the remote host (check the remote directory).

tools.example:
runfeko horn -np            -> ERROR 20003 (number of processes must follow -np)
runfeko horn -np 8 --machines-file   -> ERROR 20012
Fix: runfeko horn -np 8 --machines-file hosts.list
Check MPI setup: envfeko --plain | findstr FEKO_WHICH_MPI
tools.notes: Numbers and texts verified in the RUNFEKO section of the installed 2026.1 reference. On this install envfeko reports FEKO_WHICH_MPI=11 with Intel MPI under ...\2026.1\common\mpi\win64. ERROR 20134/20135 concern newFASANT options; newFASANT left the standard installer in 2025 and the Launcher in 2025.1. From 2026.1 the parallel solver executable is feko.mpi.exe (replaces feko.csv.msmpi.exe / feko.csv.impi.exe) - update scripts that call MPI executables directly.

tools.name: PREFEKO input-file errors (ERROR 30007, 30468, include files, EG/EN cards)
tools.description: PREFEKO converts the .pre (plus .cfm) into the .fek and stops on file-system and syntax problems. File errors: 23055/30007/30524 error creating a temporary file, 30468 error opening the input file, 30361/30409/30477/30679/30772 error opening an include file, 30006 file name too long, 30411 .cfm version newer than this PREFEKO can read. Card-structure errors: 30092 only one EG card, 30093 only one EN card at the very end, 30252/30896 EN card missing after the AC/AW card, 30110 tab character in the input file, 30932 line too long, 30707 undefined variable, 30046/30047 IP card missing or with zero segment/edge length.
tools.usage: prefeko model [options]  (normally run automatically by runfeko); messages on the 'Executing prefeko' dialog and in the terminal

parameters.name: ERROR 30007 (also 23055, 30524)
parameters.description: Temporary file cannot be created: check write permission and free space in the model folder and the Feko temp folder (FEKO_TMPDIR, shown by envfeko).

parameters.name: ERROR 30468
parameters.description: The input .pre cannot be opened: wrong name or folder, or file locked.

parameters.name: ERROR 30411
parameters.description: This PREFEKO cannot read the .cfm file version; use matching CADFEKO and PREFEKO versions.

parameters.name: WARNING 30004
parameters.description: The licence does not support ASCII .fek files.

tools.example:
prefeko dipole
ERROR 30093: Only one EN card may be used in the input file, at the very end.
Fix: remove the extra EN line (often inside an INCLUDEd file), keep one EN as the last card, rerun: runfeko dipole
tools.notes: Texts verified in the PREFEKO section of the installed 2026.1 reference (30007 also seen from prefeko). envfeko on this install reports FEKO_TMPDIR=C:\Temp; the folder must exist and be writable. Since 2026.1 CADFEKO Save writes only the .cfx; the .pre/.cfm are written when a solver component is launched or via Export > Solver input files (Ctrl+J), so a stale or missing .pre can surface here.

tools.name: GPU notes and warnings (NOTE 35179, WARNING 35146, 35204, 40271)
tools.description: With a compatible NVIDIA card present but GPU use not requested, the solver prints NOTE 35179 (use --use-gpu or the GUI checkbox). When GPU use is requested, initialisation problems give WARNING 35146 (no compatible NVIDIA GPU), 35204 (--use-gpu used but no NVIDIA driver nvcuda.dll found), 35147 (CUDA BLAS could not be initialised), 40110/40111 (CUDA driver initialisation failed, GPU deactivated), 40270/40271 (unsupported or no compatible CUDA device) and NOTE 35157/40183 (no double precision on the GPU, switching to CPU). ERROR 40169-40173 reject malformed --use-gpu device lists, 40181 is a device-memory allocation failure, 50193 lists RL-GO cases without GPU support and 40503 (FDTD) suggests adjusting CUDA_CACHE_MAXSIZE.
tools.usage: runfeko model --use-gpu [NUM_GPUS][:GPU_1[,GPU_N]]   |   runfeko model --use-gpu 0 (disables GPU detection)   |   CADFEKO: Solve/Run > Run/Launch dialog launcher > Component Launch Options

parameters.name: --use-gpu 0
parameters.description: Suppresses the GPU-detection NOTE 35179.

parameters.name: --use-gpu 2:0,2
parameters.description: Two GPUs, devices 0 and 2; the count and list must agree (ERROR 40173), no duplicates (40172), indices in range (40171).

parameters.name: ERROR 50193
parameters.description: GPU RL-GO is not supported for automatic mode settings, curvilinear triangle meshes, receiving antennas, ground planes or when coupled to a MoM region.

parameters.name: NOTEs 40402-48708 (FDTD)
parameters.description: GPU deactivated for FDTD with Liao boundaries, CPML of 16 or more cells, unsupported time signals, time-domain far fields, dispersive media or modal ports.

tools.example:
NOTE 35179: Compatible graphics card (GPU) found on this machine for possible hardware acceleration. Please use the command-line option --use-gpu ...
-> use it:   runfeko model --use-gpu 1
-> silence:  runfeko model --use-gpu 0
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; '--use-gpu 0' suppressing NOTE 35179 verified locally. The 2025.1 release notes state CUDA 12.8 (Windows driver 527.41 or newer, compute capability 7.0 or higher) and OptiX 9.0 for ray tracing (driver R570 or newer). 2026 added multi-GPU CMA; 2026.1 added GPU acceleration of the FEM and FEM/MoM direct sparse solver (single node, multi-GPU).

tools.name: Licence errors and termination signals (Error Signal 34017, 3616, 3617, 3622)
tools.description: The solver reports abnormal termination as 'Error Signal' messages: 34017 the process was terminated due to a licence error, 3616 by Ctrl-C, 3622 by Ctrl-Break and 3617 by kill. Feature-level licence messages are ERROR 4334 (advanced FEM preconditioners not licensed), NOTE 53259 (radiation source imaging not licensed), WARNING 32292 (no superuser mode) and PREFEKO WARNING 30004 (ASCII .fek files not licensed). During an iterative solution one Ctrl-C only stops the iterations (NOTE 33458, then WARNING 33459: computation continues with the current, possibly wrong solution); repeat it to terminate Feko.
tools.usage: .out file / console; check what licence path Feko sees with 'envfeko --plain' (ALTAIR_LICENSE_PATH) and the Altair licence tools

parameters.name: Error Signal 34017
parameters.description: Licence checkout failed or was lost: verify licence server or file and available units, then rerun.

parameters.name: NOTE 33458 / WARNING 33459
parameters.description: Manual stop of the iterations; later results may be wrong.

tools.example:
Error Signal 34017: Feko process was terminated due to a licence error.
Check: envfeko --plain | findstr ALTAIR_LICENSE_PATH
Retry with fewer processes (runfeko model -np 1) to rule out running out of units.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; envfeko output verified locally (here ALTAIR_LICENSE_PATH points to ...\2026.1\security\altair_lic.dat). The 2026 release notes state that solver-integrated adaptive frequency sampling needs fewer licence checks than the old ADAPTFEKO loop. Feko Student Edition limits are not documented in the local 2026.1 help.

tools.name: Segmentation-rule errors: elements too large (ERROR 114, 120, 2367, 2368)
tools.description: The solver checks element size against the wavelength. ERROR 114 (wire segment too long), 120/32971 (triangle too large), 257/502 (cuboid too large) and 4450/4455/4796 (tetrahedron too large) mean the mesh is too coarse for the frequency; WARNINGs 115, 121, 258/503 and 4451/4456/4797 report coarse but accepted segmentation and 1663/33131 and 1664 inhomogeneous segmentation. ERROR 2367/2368 (triangle or segment too large, or model tolerance too small), 4681 with WARNING 4682 (waveguide-port triangles too large for the included modes) and 38014/WARNING 38015 (LE-PO triangles too large with near-field requests) belong to the same family.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Mesh tab > Find group > Oversized Elements to locate offenders; Mesh > Meshing > Create Mesh with a smaller size or local mesh size on faces/edges; Mesh > Refinement Rules; or lower the maximum frequency

parameters.name: Mesh size
parameters.description: The resource-reduction tips cite lambda/10 (free-space wavelength) as the standard mesh size; coarser meshes only in low-current or shadow regions.

parameters.name: WARNING 45010
parameters.description: Frequency-dependent mesh element size checking is switched off (CADFEKO Solver Settings > General > 'Activate mesh element size checking', EG card), so these errors are not raised.

tools.example:
ERROR 120: Segmentation rules have been violated (triangle is too large).
Fix: Mesh > Find > Oversized Elements with Length = c0/fmax/10, set a Local mesh size on those faces (face Properties > Meshing tab), remesh and rerun.
tools.notes: Message texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; the lambda/10 figure and 'coarser only where currents are small' come from the 'How to reduce resources - General tips' page; the Oversized Elements tool from the CADFEKO user guide. Do not switch off mesh-size checking to hide the error.

tools.name: Elements too small, too short or too thick (ERROR 240, 241, 33270, 116, 3632)
tools.description: Vertices closer than the model tolerance (EG card 'Maximum identical distance') are treated as one point, so elements smaller than it are rejected: ERROR 240 (triangle smaller than the tolerance), 241 (segment too short or tolerance too large), 33270 (triangle edge too short), 4043/4686 (tetrahedron or tetrahedron edge too small) and 2004/2005 (cylinder height/radius below the tolerance). Wires have their own limits: ERROR 116 (segment radius-to-length ratio too large), 3632 (ratio too small), 629 (zero radius), 2701 (wire at a connection point too thick for the triangle size) and WARNING 3915 (extreme length ratio of two segments at a node). Tiny CAD features such as sliver faces and short edges are the usual source.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Transform tab > Repair group > Remove Small Features or Repair Part ('Remove small edges'); Mesh tab > Find group > Distorted Elements; EDITFEKO: EG card 'Maximum identical distance', IP card segment radius

parameters.name: Model tolerance
parameters.description: EG card 'Maximum identical distance': points closer than this are connected; ERROR 240/241/33270 fire for elements below it.

parameters.name: Wire radius vs segment length
parameters.description: Keep the radius well below the segment length (ERROR 116) but non-zero (ERROR 629); thick wires at surface junctions trigger 2701.

tools.example:
ERROR 241: A segment is too short or the model tolerance is too large.
Fix: take the element number from the .out, locate it with POSTFEKO Find Elements, remove the short edge in CADFEKO (Repair Part with 'Remove small edges' or delete/merge the tiny geometry), remesh.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; the tolerance meaning from the EG card page and the repair options from the CADFEKO Repair Part page (2026.1 user guide).

tools.name: Mesh connectivity errors (ERROR 832, 835, 2712, 178, 180)
tools.description: Feko connects elements only where they share edges and vertices. ERROR 832 (two triangles touch without a common edge), 835 (two segments touch without a common node), 2712/39997/52582 (segmentation rules at a wire-surface connection point violated), 178 (triangle with neither an edge basis function nor a connection point), 180 (segment with neither a node nor a connection point) and WARNING 555 (segment and triangle connected in different media) point to non-conformal meshes. The EG card page names the typical user errors that normal geometry checking finds: a wire connected to the middle of another wire where the points do not coincide, and surfaces with different segmentation along a common edge.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Construct tab > Modify group > Union (and Transform tab > Imprint group > Imprint Points / Project) before meshing; Mesh tab > Repair group > Merge Vertices for imported meshes; keep Solver Settings > General > 'Activate normal geometry checking' on

parameters.name: Activate normal geometry checking
parameters.description: Verifies identical triangle edge lengths on connecting surfaces, coincident connection points, appropriate element sizes and segment length-to-radius ratios.

parameters.name: Domain Connectivity
parameters.description: Solve/Run > Solution Settings > Domain Connectivity lets MoM and MoM/MLFMM treat nearby, non-coincident mesh borders as connected (e.g. antenna on an imported platform mesh).

tools.example:
ERROR 832: Segmentation rules have been violated (two triangles touch without a common edge).
Fix: select the touching parts, Construct > Modify > Union, remesh; for imported meshes use Mesh > Repair > Merge Vertices with a small tolerance.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; geometry-check contents from the CADFEKO 'General Solver Settings' page and the EG card page.

tools.name: Overlapping and intersecting elements (ERROR 499, 2331, 4442, 4443, 4562)
tools.description: Overlapping geometry creates duplicate unknowns and is rejected: ERROR 499 (two segments overlap), 2331 (two triangular patches overlap), 4441/4444/4517 and 4562 (tetrahedra overlap), 4442 (coincident tetrahedra), 4443 (boundary surfaces of a FEM region intersect), 4563 (triangle and tetrahedron overlap), 543 (dielectric/magnetic cuboids overlap) and 46029 (two ports overlap). They usually come from duplicated imported meshes, parts copied on top of each other, or intersecting parts that were not unioned. WARNING 33563 means frequency-independent geometry checking (mesh overlaps etc.) was switched off, so such overlaps go undetected.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Mesh tab > Find group > Intersecting Triangles / Clashing Geometry; Mesh > Repair > Remove Duplicates; Construct > Modify > Union; keep 'Activate normal geometry checking' enabled (EG card 'Switch normal geometry checking off' unchecked)

parameters.name: Intersecting Triangles
parameters.description: Searches the entire model or a selection; results appear in Model Status and the Message Details dialog with hyperlinks, offending parts are selected.

parameters.name: Clashing Geometry
parameters.description: Finds geometry parts that clash before meshing.

tools.example:
ERROR 2331: Two triangular surface patches overlap.
Fix: Mesh > Find > Intersecting Triangles, delete the duplicate part or union the clashing parts, remesh and rerun.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; Find tool behaviour verified in the CADFEKO 2026.1 user guide ('Searching for Intersecting Mesh Elements' notes that imported meshes often contain them).

tools.name: Closed-surface and normal-vector errors (ERROR 33462, 4435, 35382, 52000-52003)
tools.description: Volume and body formulations need closed, consistently oriented boundaries. FEM regions: ERROR 33462 (dielectric FEM body without a closed surface; results wrong unless the fields at the opening are zero), 52258/52259 (FEM body not closed), WARNING 4542 (FEM region surface inconsistent), 4435 (unconnected tetrahedron), WARNING 4445 (flat tetrahedra compromise accuracy). Bodies: 35382/39981/39982 (CFIE/MFIE/thick-coating body not closed), 39977/39986 (SEP body not closed), 33457 (inconsistent normal specification), 52000-52003 (normals must point consistently towards the source region), 3864 (media inconsistent with normal orientation) and WARNING 56022 (triangles with opposite normals).
tools.usage: CADFEKO: build closed solids and union them before meshing; Transform tab > Alter group > Reverse Normals; Transform > Repair > Repair and Sew Faces for open imported sheets; check media with the validation colouring

parameters.name: CFIE / MFIE
parameters.description: Only on closed PEC bodies; normals point outwards when sources are outside (52001) and inwards when all sources are inside (52002).

parameters.name: FEM region
parameters.description: Must be a closed volume of tetrahedra connected to the rest of the mesh (4435).

tools.example:
ERROR 52000: The normal vectors on a CFIE/MFIE/thick coating body must consistently point outwards towards the source region.
Fix: select the faces, Transform > Alter > Reverse Normals (or rebuild as one closed solid), remesh, rerun.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; the MLFMM convergence how-to adds that CFIE applies only to surfaces bounding closed PEC structures and that sharp corners on CFIE surfaces need finer meshing or EFIE.

tools.name: Singular matrix errors (ERROR 103, 562, 4724, 4726; WARNING 104, 563)
tools.description: The MoM system cannot be solved because the matrix is singular (ERROR 103/562) or is numerically singular (WARNING 104/563, 'solution very critical'); ERROR 4724/4726 add the recommendation to try double precision, and 37181/37182 and 37195/37196 are the NGF static/dynamic interaction-matrix equivalents. Causes include duplicated or overlapping elements, distorted (sliver) triangles, very small electrical size and single precision on ill-conditioned problems. The CADFEKO help notes that distorted elements raise the MoM condition number and that the solver warns or stops when it becomes too high, which can also happen at very low frequencies.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Solve/Run > Solution Settings > Solver Settings > General: data storage precision double; Mesh tab > Find group > Distorted Elements (minimum internal angle) and Intersecting Triangles; low-frequency stabilisation for electrically tiny models

parameters.name: Double precision
parameters.description: Twice the memory of the default single precision; reduces numerical noise.

parameters.name: Distorted Elements
parameters.description: Lists triangles with an internal angle below the given minimum; remove slivers by deleting mesh vertices or redundant geometry points.

tools.example:
ERROR 4724: The MoM matrix is singular, no solution possible. It is recommended to try double precision accuracy (Solver Settings).
Fix: Solver Settings > double precision; Mesh > Find > Distorted Elements and Intersecting Triangles, clean up, remesh, rerun.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; condition-number remarks and sliver advice from 'Searching for Distorted Mesh Elements' (CADFEKO 2026.1 user guide).

tools.name: Iterative solver non-convergence (WARNING 830, 831, 48600; ERROR 33498, 36002)
tools.description: MLFMM, FEM and hybrid solutions are iterative. WARNING 830/831 (no convergence; the solution with the smallest residuum is used), 48600 (stagnation), 48709 (restart limit), 49026 (stabilised MLFMM), 32996 (hybrid MoM/PO) and 36496 (stopping criterion may be insufficient) mean results can be inaccurate; ERROR 33498, 36002 (residuum diverges), 48601 (stagnated) and 48710 stop the run, and the how-to guides quote ERROR 4673 (iterative solution failed, try another preconditioner). Per the MLFMM how-to, a radiating antenna's impedance is often still acceptable after WARNING 830, whereas RCS at low-backscatter angles is not.
tools.usage: MLFMM remedies (how-to 'Improve Convergence for the MLFMM'): adjust the mesh, change the preconditioner, change the finest MLFMM box size, apply CFIE to closed PEC bodies, use double precision, activate the stabilised MLFMM (metallic triangles only); set in CADFEKO Solve/Run > Solution Settings > Solver Settings

parameters.name: Preconditioner
parameters.description: Sparse LU is the default (most memory); SPAI accelerated (fast) or non-accelerated (slower, often converges better); DLP converges better with fewer processes, which 2026.1 mitigates.

parameters.name: Box size
parameters.description: Default 0.23 wavelength; try 0.2 to 0.35 in steps of 0.03 (larger uses more memory).

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Small changes to element size can help; overly fine or coarse meshes hurt convergence; reduce radii of thick wires or replace them with strips/cylinders.

parameters.name: Iterative solver
parameters.description: FGMRES is the default for MLFMM and FEM/FEM-MLFMM since 2025.1; 2026.1 adds the Advanced Iterative Solver (AIS, Solver Settings > Advanced / CG card) with lower memory but possibly longer runtime.

tools.example:
WARNING 830: Maximum number of iterations reached without convergence ... solution with the smallest residuum ...
Steps: 1) preconditioner -> SPAI (non-accelerated)  2) MLFMM box size 0.26  3) CFIE on closed PEC parts  4) double precision; rerun and compare results.
tools.notes: Message texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; remedies verified in the 2026.1 how-tos for MLFMM and MLFMM/FEM convergence (ERROR 4673 is quoted there but is not listed in the 2026.1 Errors reference). 2026.1 interim results (FP card / Solver Settings > Advanced) store results at relaxed residuum levels so POSTFEKO can show whether convergence matters.

tools.name: FEM, MoM/FEM and FDTD convergence remedies (ERROR 4673, WARNING 48135, ERROR 48147)
tools.description: For hybrid MoM/FEM the how-to lists: adjust the mesh, switch the preconditioner from the default multilevel LU/diagonal decomposition to multilevel ILU/diagonal (fill-in per row 200, stabilisation factor 1) or to LU of the FEM matrix (EDITFEKO CG card only), use double precision, use first-order FEM basis functions, or use the direct sparse FEM solver, which avoids iterative convergence problems. MLFMM/FEM adds the MLFMM box size and CFIE options. FDTD runs report WARNING 48135 (may not be converged) or ERROR 48147 (did not converge); the FDTD how-to recommends a 50 ohm load at the feed, a 5-10 times longer total time interval, dielectric losses, double precision, 'Use intrinsic wire radius' for wire ports, or swapping wire and edge feeds.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Solve/Run > Solution Settings > Solver Settings (FEM / FDTD options); EDITFEKO: CG card (preconditioner, FGMRES / AIS), FP card

parameters.name: FEM element order
parameters.description: Default auto; since 2026 chosen per region from the electrical element size (first order for electrically very small elements). Forcing first order can help convergence.

parameters.name: Direct sparse FEM solver
parameters.description: Non-iterative, so no convergence failure; GPU accelerated on a single node in 2026.1.

parameters.name: FDTD 50 ohm load
parameters.description: Speeds convergence; remove its effect on impedance with 'Subtract loading' in the POSTFEKO result palette (gain drops, directivity unchanged).

parameters.name: FDTD total time interval
parameters.description: The value used internally is printed in the .out; increase 5-10 times if the signal has not propagated through the domain.

tools.example:
WARNING 48135: Finite difference time domain solution may not be converged.
Steps: add a 50 ohm load on the feed port, set the time interval to 5x its value, rerun; in POSTFEKO tick 'Subtract loading' when plotting impedance.
tools.notes: Verified in the 2026.1 how-to pages 'Improve Convergence for the MoM / FEM', '... MLFMM / FEM' and '... FDTD'; message numbers verified in the installed reference. FGMRES became the default FEM/FEM-MLFMM iterative solver in 2025.1.

tools.name: Out-of-memory errors (ERROR 32463, 997, 4039, 33238; NOTE 33242, 48414)
tools.description: 'Not enough memory available for dynamic allocation' is shared by a long list of numbers (296 ... 32463 ...); specific variants cover the MoM matrix (997/1036), FEM matrices and preconditioners (4039, 4357, 4467, 4475/4476, 4615, 32460), in-core-only cases (33132 with FEM, 37307 with NGF, 37583 with CMA, 55185 with CBFM), the sparse LU workspace (48171), MUMPS (48173/48214) and a full disk for out-of-core files (33238, 3356). NOTE 33242/33243 say single precision can avoid the allocation error for MLFMM, and NOTEs 4574/4616/4617/33175/33178 report that the MoM matrix was released or arrays swapped to disk. Estimate requirements first with --estimate-resource-requirements-only, which ends the .out with NOTE 48414 and 'Memory estimate for a regular Feko run'.
tools.usage: runfeko model -np N [--machines-file m] --feko-options --estimate-resource-requirements-only   (CADFEKO: Solve/Run > Run/Launch > Feko Terminal)

parameters.name: Preconditioner
parameters.description: Sparse LU (MLFMM default) needs the most memory; SPAI or ILU need less; DLP estimates lie between SPAI and sparse LU.

parameters.name: Precision
parameters.description: Single precision (default) uses half the memory of double.

parameters.name: Estimate accuracy
parameters.description: Needs roughly 1/30 to 1/3 of the full-run memory; a memory error during the estimate means the full run fails with the same processes/hosts; far-field requests are not included; use the intended machines file.

tools.example:
runfeko car_a -np 40 --machines-file hosts.list --feko-options --estimate-resource-requirements-only
...

tools.name: Source, port and symmetry errors (ERROR 15, 34401, 16-21, 221, 4681, 35135)
tools.description: Excitation errors: ERROR 15 (no source defined), 34401 (S-parameter request but no source), 174/48234 (frequency too small or not defined), 16/17 (undefined wire port segment or node/connection point), 18 (wire port not allowed at this vertex), 21 (metallic edge for an edge port does not exist), 46029 (two ports overlap). Port geometry errors: 4657/4971 (waveguide-port triangle normals inconsistent with the port direction), 4681/WARNING 4682 (waveguide-port mesh too coarse for the modes), 4789/WARNING 4790 (FEM line port too long for the wavelength), 36197 (modal-port modes not orthogonal). Symmetry errors: 221-230 and others (excitation contradicts the symmetry), 35124/35135 (geometry not symmetric), 2577 (no electric/magnetic symmetry with MLFMM), 4972 (unsymmetrical waveguide port).

parameters.name: Symmetry
parameters.description: Electric/magnetic symmetry requires the complete geometry and excitation to be symmetric; with MLFMM only geometric symmetry is allowed and gives no memory saving.

parameters.name: Waveguide / FEM ports
parameters.description: Mesh the port face fine enough for the modes; orient all port-triangle normals the same way; shorten FEM line ports relative to the wavelength.

tools.example:
ERROR 15: No source has been defined.
Fix: Source/Load > Sources on Ports > Voltage Source on Port1 in the active configuration (or use an S-parameter configuration with active ports), rerun.
tools.notes: All texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference. Only activate the ports you need in S-parameter configurations: each active port is an extra solution (general resource tips).

tools.name: Stale solution-file messages (.mat/.lud/.ngf/.str/.vis: 33204, 33206, 4715, 3266)
tools.description: Feko can reuse stored matrices (.mat, .lud), numerical Green's function data (.ngf), solution coefficients (.str) and PO visibility/shadowing data (.vis, .sha). If the model changed since they were written you get 33204 (file found for a solution that has changed), 33206, 46100-46102 and 46119-46122 (file does not match the current solution), 3266 (.vis does not match the geometry), WARNING 33263 (.sha does not match), WARNING 4495 (*_fem.mat for a changed solution) and NOTE 33047/35441 (.str for a different FEM region). Precision mismatches give 4715/46117 and 4871 (single/double precision setting incompatible with the stored file).
tools.usage: Delete the stale files next to the model, or clear the corresponding 'Save / read' option on the PS card (EDITFEKO: Request tab > Output control > Data structures (PS)), and rerun; keep the precision setting unchanged when reusing .mat/.lud/.ngf

parameters.name: .str reuse
parameters.description: Lets you add or change output requests without re-solving; only valid while geometry and excitation are unchanged.

parameters.name: WARNING 33268
parameters.description: The parallel version does not use .sha PO shadowing files.

tools.example:
ERROR 33206: The .mat, .ngf or .lud file does not match the current solution.
Fix: del model.mat model.lud model.ngf  then  runfeko model
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; .str reuse purpose from 'Read MAT, LUD, RHS and STR Files' and the general resource tips (2026.1 user guide). Inspect a .str with str2ascii.

tools.name: High-frequency method validity messages (PO, LE-PO, RL-GO, UTD: 40617, 40752, 33719, 47012)
tools.description: Asymptotic methods need electrically large regions: ERROR 40617/WARNING 40751 (PO/LE-PO triangle area too small), 40752/WARNING 40753 (RL-GO area too small) and 40754/WARNING 40755 (faceted UTD area too small) all recommend a full-wave solver (MoM, MLFMM, FEM or FDTD) instead. Setup conflicts include 33719 (RL-GO requested but no RL-GO triangles), 2579 (MLFMM and UTD/RL-GO in the same model), 32455 (UTD/RL-GO with FEM), 33676 (RL-GO and UTD together) and 33661 (UTD/RL-GO with cable modelling). Accuracy warnings: 47012 (triangles treated as planar because edges are very short compared with the wavelength - check the mesh), 40739 (RL-GO rays did not reach the convergence level), 49004 (switched to the iterative MoM/PO hybrid) and 32996 (hybrid MoM/PO did not converge).
tools.usage: CADFEKO: set the solution method per face/region (face or region properties) and the high-frequency options in Solve/Run > Solution Settings > Solver Settings (High Frequency tab); keep MoM/MLFMM on small parts

parameters.name: RL-GO fixed grid (2026.1)
parameters.description: Simplified to one angular and one spatial increment; ERROR 47020-47023 report increments that are too small.

parameters.name: Model Status check (2026)
parameters.description: CADFEKO flags a region too small relative to the wavelength for an asymptotic method before solving.

tools.example:
ERROR 40752: Total area of RL-GO triangles is too small for the high frequency approximation to be valid. Please use a full wave solver ...
Fix: set the small part back to MoM (or MLFMM) and keep RL-GO only on the electrically large platform.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference; the Model Status check and RL-GO grid change are from the 2026 and 2026.1 release notes.

tools.name: OPTFEKO messages (ERROR 21010, WARNING 21049, 21293, 21382)
tools.description: OPTFEKO errors include 21010 (file not found), 21018/21084 (error writing or closing a file), 21068 (MD5 checksums of <name>_opt_N.bof and .fek do not match), 21295 (invalid number of parallel processes from the machines file), 21324/21325 (GA population must be at least 2, PSO at least 1), 21368 (method not supported with HyperOpt) and 33866 (HyperOpt not supported on this platform). Warnings: 21049/21051/21367 maximum number of analyses reached (possible premature convergence), 21293/21294 farming limited by the PSO/GA population size, 21098 Simplex farms only while building a new simplex, 21327 grid search with very many analyses, 21382 ARSM does not support farming, 21383 GRSM reduces farming processes to reach its minimum iterations, and 21122 existing results cannot be reused.
tools.usage: optfeko model [options]; CADFEKO: Solve/Run > Run/Launch > OPTFEKO; messages on the 'Executing optfeko' dialog

parameters.name: WARNING 21049/21051/21367
parameters.description: Raise the maximum number of solver runs or tighten the search bounds; the result may not be optimal.

parameters.name: RUNFEKO ERROR 20088
parameters.description: Optimisation with continuous (adaptive) frequency data is not supported; use discrete frequencies.

tools.example:
WARNING 21293: Optimisation will only use 5 parallel processes due to the PSO population size.
Fix: increase the PSO population size in the optimisation search, or accept the reduced farming.
tools.notes: All numbers and texts verified in the OPTFEKO section of the installed 2026.1 reference.

tools.name: Adaptive frequency sampling messages (ADAPTFEKO section, 31005-31155)
tools.description: The messages guide keeps an ADAPTFEKO section for the adaptive (continuous) frequency sampling component; since Feko 2026 this sampling runs inside the solver and 2026.1 ships no adaptfeko executable. Setup errors: 31011 minimum frequency must be above zero, 31012 maximum must exceed minimum, 31013 more than two frequency points required, 31045 only one AC card, 31055 FR and AC card together, 31121 continuous frequency not supported with FDTD, 31061/31074 run terminated due to an error in RUNFEKO (see the preceding solver error). Warnings: 31005 maximum number of sample points reached, 31062 a frequency subinterval did not converge, 31096/31097 minimum frequency stepping reached (possibly not converged), 31083 no calculation requests, 31123 characteristic-mode results not used.
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Source/Load > Settings > Frequency: continuous (interpolated) range (2026.1: optional frequencies of interest); EDITFEKO: FR card continuous-data option

parameters.name: WARNING 31005 / 31062
parameters.description: Increase the maximum number of samples or narrow the band, and verify resonances with a few discrete frequencies.

parameters.name: RUNFEKO ERROR 20063
parameters.description: --adaptfeko-mode must be followed by the frequency number being analysed.

tools.example:
WARNING 31062: ADAPTFEKO: Frequency subinterval 3 of 5 has not converged.
Fix: raise the maximum number of samples (or split the band) and rerun; check the flagged subinterval with discrete points.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the ADAPTFEKO section of the installed 2026.1 reference. The 2026 release notes: sampling integrated into the solver (PREFEKO once, fewer licence checks, usable with AMRFEKO) and ADAPTFEKO settings removed from Component Launch Options. 2026.1 adds frequencies of interest, on-the-fly .afs export, seed frequencies and .str reuse. The general tips warn that continuous sampling with many requests (e.g. all currents) can be slow.

tools.name: Cable and MTL placement messages (ERROR 38287, 39693, 52912; WARNING 38625)
tools.description: Multiconductor transmission line (MTL) theory assumes cables run close to and along a conducting surface. ERROR 38287 (cable path must be within 0.2 wavelengths of a conducting surface), 39693 (cable end point within 0.2 wavelengths of a metallic triangle/segment/PEC ground; use a finer mesh around cable ends), WARNING 38625/38953 (segments farther than 0.1 wavelengths; quasi-TEM assumption may be violated), 39439 (segment should run roughly parallel to the nearby surface), 39442 (over 10 percent of segments badly oriented) and 52473 (over 2 percent at an extreme orientation) enforce this. Geometric conflicts: 52912 (cable path intersects a conducting surface), 39438 (geometry intersects a cable cross section), 38139/38178 (cable height above ground too small), 39063/39066 (path sections overlap) and WARNING 39064 (sections intersect).
tools.usage: CADFEKO: Home > Extensions > Cables, then Cables tab > Definitions > Cable Path; keep paths close to and parallel with the structure; refine the mesh near cable end points (Mesh > Refinement Rules > Point Refinement)

parameters.name: 0.2 / 0.1 wavelength limits
parameters.description: Error above 0.2 wavelengths from a conducting surface; warning above 0.1 wavelengths.

parameters.name: Path sections
parameters.description: Split cable paths into non-overlapping sections (39063/39066).

tools.example:
ERROR 39693: A cable end point should be defined within 0.2 wavelengths of a metallic triangle/segment/PEC ground plane. Please use a finer mesh around such cable end points.
Fix: move the path end onto the chassis or add a point refinement there, remesh, rerun.
tools.notes: Texts verified in the installed 2026.1 reference. The 2026.1 release notes fix the cable installation search radius for an infinite PEC ground at non-zero z.

tools.name: CADFEKO geometry faults: remove and recreate the faulty entity
tools.description: When importing geometry, CADFEKO reports Parasolid body faults on the Importing file dialog. For most faults, which the reference attributes to importing and in particular scaled importing, the advice is to select the faulty entity (in the details tree), remove it and recreate it. Missing geometry arises only with imported models; the entity is not visible in the 3D view and has to be recreated.
tools.usage: Importing file dialog after Home > File > Import; select the entity in the details tree > delete > recreate; try Transform tab > Repair group > Repair Part first

parameters.name: Missing geometry / Invalid geometry
parameters.description: Remove the faulty entity (not visible in the 3D view) and recreate it.

parameters.name: Self-intersecting or degenerate geometry; Geometry not G1-continuous
parameters.description: Usually scaled importing; remove and recreate.

parameters.name: Vertex not on curve of edge / not on nominal geometry / not on surface of face
parameters.description: Remove and recreate the entity.

parameters.name: Vertices of edge touch
parameters.description: Remove and recreate; the whole face may have to be deleted to remove the faulty edge.

parameters.name: Loops inconsistent; Missing vertex at surface singularity; Face-face inconsistency
parameters.description: Remove and recreate the entity.

parameters.name: B-geometry has knots closer than the allowed precision
parameters.description: Most probably scaled importing; remove and recreate.

tools.example:
Import of bracket.step reports 'Vertex not on surface of face':
1) Transform > Repair > Repair Part on the imported part
2) if the fault remains, delete that face and rebuild it (e.g. Construct > Create Surface, then Construct > Modify > Union), remesh.
tools.notes: Fault names and advice verified in the installed 2026.1 'CADFEKO Geometry Faults' page; the CAD fixing tools overview recommends running the fixing tools directly after import, starting with Repair Part. Because scaled importing is the usual cause, re-importing without a scale factor is worth trying (inference, not stated in the reference).

tools.name: CADFEKO geometry faults: explode/recombine, import-only and support cases
tools.description: Some import faults can be fixed by exploding the part and combining the entities again: Faces incorrectly ordered at edge, Edge not on surface of face, Self-intersecting face (edge/edge inconsistency) and Edges incorrectly ordered at vertex. Others only occur with imported models: Invalid or duplicate identifiers (old Parasolid models), Edge reversed, Nominal geometry in wrong direction, Body is inside out, and Non-printing character in an attribute name (work can continue). Faults that should not arise must be reported with the original model file (in its original format) to Feko support: Corrupt data structures, Open or non-periodic curve or nominal geometry attached to ring edge (import or stitching), SP-curve tolerance faults, Wire-frame edge/face and edge/edge inconsistencies (unions of wires with faced bodies), Size-box violation, inconsistent shells or regions, Geometry/topology inconsistency in shell, Acorn shell/shell inconsistency, and Unspecified checker failure.
tools.usage: Transform tab > Alter group > Explode, then Construct tab > Modify group > Union or Stitch; for support cases send the original CAD file to Feko support

parameters.name: Explode and recombine
parameters.description: Faces incorrectly ordered at edge; Edge not on surface of face; Self-intersecting face; Edges incorrectly ordered at vertex.

parameters.name: Import-only
parameters.description: Invalid or duplicate identifiers; Edge reversed; Nominal geometry in wrong direction; Body is inside out; Non-printing character used in name of attribute definition.

parameters.name: Report to support
parameters.description: Corrupt data structures (translation failed or source model faulty); ring-edge curve faults; SP-curve faults; wire-frame inconsistencies; size-box; shell/region faults; checker failures (work may continue but undetected faults may remain).

tools.example:
Import reports 'Edges incorrectly ordered at vertex':
1) select the part, Transform > Alter > Explode
2) select the resulting faces, Construct > Modify > Stitch (or Union)
3) re-check: remesh and look at Home > Validate > Model Status
tools.notes: Fault names and advice verified in the installed 2026.1 'CADFEKO Geometry Faults' page; ribbon locations verified in the CADFEKO user guide.

tools.name: CAD fixing tools (Repair Part, Repair Edges, Repair and Sew Faces)
tools.description: The CAD fixing tools heal imported bodies so they can be meshed. Repair Part attempts to fix invalid topology sense, invalid edge/vertex tolerances, invalid, self-intersecting or non-G1 geometry, missing edge/vertex geometry or vertices, and vertices or edges not on their curves/surfaces; the repaired part is renamed RepairPart1. Repair Edges recalculates tolerant edges and vertices to a linear tolerance and merges redundant edges; Repair and Sew Faces heals faces, removes faces with bad trimming curves and sews the rest into a sheet or solid.
tools.usage: Transform tab > Repair group > Repair Part | Repair Edges | Repair and Sew Faces | Remove Small Features | Simplify Part Representation; Transform tab > Rebuild group > Fill Hole

parameters.name: Remove small edges / Maximum length of small edges
parameters.description: Repair Part: removes edges shorter than the given arc length (fixes tolerance errors from tiny edges).

parameters.name: Upper bound on deviation between original and repaired geometry
parameters.description: Repair Part tolerance; optional more lenient Edge repair tolerance.

parameters.name: Remove self-intersections / Remove discontinuities
parameters.description: Split or smooth surfaces; angular tolerance decides between smoothing and splitting at G1 discontinuities.

parameters.name: Repair bad face-face errors; simplification options
parameters.description: Fix face-face collisions; simplify B-surfaces/curves to analytic forms, rational to non-rational, high-degree B-geometry to cubic.

parameters.name: Linear tolerance for repairing / Merge edges
parameters.description: Repair Edges settings.

tools.example:
1) Home > File > Import > bracket.stp
2) Transform > Repair > Repair Part (default settings) -> RepairPart1
3) if faces are still open: Transform > Repair > Repair and Sew Faces
4) Mesh > Create Mesh, check Home > Validate > Model Status
tools.notes: Verified in the CADFEKO 2026.1 user guide (CAD Fixing Tools Overview, Repair Part, Repair Edges, Repair and Sew Faces). Guidance: apply directly after import, try Repair Part first, several tools may be needed in succession, use the smallest possible tolerance; tolerances are in the model unit.

tools.name: RUNMGRFEKO (run manager: model lists and parameter sweeps)
tools.description: New in 2026.1, RUNMGRFEKO runs batch simulations of a list of models or a parameter sweep of one model, with concurrent solver runs, farming, remote and parallel options similar to OPTFEKO but without optimisation goals. It is available from CADFEKO (Home > Run/Launch > Run Manager: List of Models or Parameter Sweep), EDITFEKO, POSTFEKO, the CADFEKO Lua API, or the command line. The input is JSON: {"version": 1, "list": [...]} for model lists or {"version": 1, "sweep": [{name, minimum, maximum, points}]} for sweeps.
tools.usage: runmgrfeko FILENAME.lst|FILENAME.swp [--run-from-gui] [-np x] [--machines-file m] [--restart n] [--runfeko-options ...] [-d<number>] [--version]

parameters.name: FILENAME
parameters.description: 2026.1 binary: must carry the extension .lst (list of files) or .swp (parameter sweep); otherwise ERROR 31423 'Expecting a filename with extension .swp or .lst'.

parameters.name: -np x
parameters.description: Number of run instances (concurrent solver executions, i.e. farming).

parameters.name: --machines-file m
parameters.description: Machines file with node names and core counts.

parameters.name: --restart n
parameters.description: Restart from task n; earlier tasks are assumed complete.

parameters.name: --runfeko-options ...
parameters.description: Options passed to RUNFEKO for each run, e.g. -np 4 parallel processes per model.

parameters.name: -d1 / -d2
parameters.description: Debug output: run control (1) and parsed input (2); bits can be summed.

tools.example:
models.lst:
{ "version": 1, "list": [ "modelA", "modelB" ] }

runmgrfeko models.lst -np 16 --machines-file hosts.list --runfeko-options -np 4

-- CADFEKO Lua (ParameterSweep API page):
sweepVar = application.Project.ParameterSweep.Variables:Append()
sweepVar.Variable = project.Definitions.Variables["freq"]
sweepVar.MinimumValue = 7e7; sweepVar.MaximumValue = 8e7; sweepVar.NumberOfGridPoints = 2
application:SaveAs(filename .. ".cfx"); project:WriteSolverInputFiles(filename .. ".cfx")
application.Project.ParameterSweep:writeToFile(filename, ".")
results = application.Launcher:RunRUNMGRFEKO(cf.Enums.RunTaskTypeEnum.Sweep)
tools.notes: Verified locally: 'runmgrfeko --help' prints the syntax above; a .lst file with the documented JSON list is parsed (-d2 shows 'Input format: List of files') and each task calls RUNFEKO (a missing model gives ERROR 20006, WARNING 31362 and ERROR 31393, exit code 99). The user guide page still describes the input as a .json file given without extension, which the 2026.1 executable rejects. RunTaskTypeEnum has List and Sweep.

tools.name: QUEUEFEKO (queuefeko_gui packages and queuefeko cluster script)
tools.description: QUEUEFEKO (binary queuefeko_gui) is a GUI that packs a model and its run settings into a .pkg package for a remote queuing system and extracts the returned package afterwards. On the cluster, the editable queuefeko console script adds the package to an execution queue such as PBS, runs the simulation and repackages the results; it is not a queuing system itself. Reusable package configuration files hold the settings: Solver or OPTFEKO launch, parallel and farmed processes, maximum RAM per process, wall-clock time, queue and e-mail notifications on start/abort/end.
tools.usage: Local: queuefeko_gui > Package > Generate package (.pkg). Cluster: queuefeko mypackage.pkg

parameters.name: Solver tab
parameters.description: Launch component (Solver or OPTFEKO), number of parallel processes, OPTFEKO restart/farming options, Advanced command-line parameters.

parameters.name: Cluster tab
parameters.description: Maximum RAM per process, maximum wall-clock time, queue, notification e-mail and events (Start, Abort, End).

tools.example:
1) queuefeko_gui: Solver tab: Launch component = Solver, 32 parallel processes; Cluster tab: RAM per process, wall-clock time, queue
2) Package > Generate package -> horn.pkg
3) on the cluster: queuefeko horn.pkg
4) copy the result package back and extract it with QUEUEFEKO
tools.notes: Verified in the installed 2026.1 QUEUEFEKO user guide pages; queuefeko_gui.exe is present in feko\bin (GUI, not launched here). The script may need edits for other queuing systems.

tools.name: str2ascii and mat2ascii (binary .str/.mat to ASCII)
tools.description: str2ascii prints a binary .str file (the MoM solution vector x of Ax = y, written by the PS card or when CADFEKO saves the solution) as ASCII on stdout; -r writes a re-parseable file with a valid header that Feko can read again (e.g. to visualise characteristic modes), -v adds header information and -c cable data. mat2ascii prints a MoM matrix .mat file for an optional block number b (typically one block per frequency; default 1); it supports only .mat files from sequential runs (parallel runs write .mat.0, .mat.1 ...).
tools.usage: str2ascii FILENAME.str [-r] [-v] [-c] > out.txt   |   mat2ascii FILENAME.mat [b] > out.txt

parameters.name: str2ascii -r
parameters.description: Re-parseable output (header plus real/imaginary coefficient pairs).

parameters.name: str2ascii -v / -c
parameters.description: Verbose header / cable data; no effect together with -r.

parameters.name: mat2ascii b
parameters.description: Block number, e.g. the frequency index; default b=1.

tools.example:
str2ascii dipole.str -r > ascii.str
mat2ascii example.mat 3 > example_fr_3.txt
tools.notes: Syntax verified by running both without arguments in 2026.1: str2ascii exits 1 with 'Please specify the name of the .str file', mat2ascii prints its usage and states a maximum supported .mat file version of 5. .mat/.lud/.rhs files are not written by default. Documented in the user guide appendix (Read the STR File, MAT2ASCII Utility).

tools.name: deembed (S-parameter port de-embedding calculator)
tools.description: Command-line utility that reads an augmented network-parameter (Touchstone) file, de-embeds selected ports using 2-port calibration networks and exports the result as a Touchstone file. Use it to remove feed lines or fixtures that were included in the Feko model from the computed S-parameters.
tools.usage: deembed FILENAME [--pall fname | --p<x> fname ...] [--export-format RI|MA] [--resultsfile fname] [--version]

parameters.name: --pall fname
parameters.description: De-embed all ports with the 2-port data in fname.

parameters.name: --p<x> fname
parameters.description: De-embed port x with the data in fname (e.g. --p1 TL_1.s2p).

parameters.name: --export-format RI|MA
parameters.description: Real/imaginary or magnitude/phase output.

parameters.name: --resultsfile fname
parameters.description: Name of the results file.

tools.example: deembed Four_Way_Power_Divider_SP.s5p --p1 TL_1_SP.s2p --p3 TL_3_SP.s2p --p4 TL_4_SP.s2p
tools.notes: Verified: running deembed without arguments in 2026.1 prints this syntax (exit code 99); the example is from the user guide page 'S-Parameter Port De-embedding Calculator'.

tools.name: multiport_processor (port re-excitation without re-solving)
tools.description: The multiport processor recomputes results for new port excitations and loads without rerunning the solver: a multiport combinations configuration (.mcc) defines the new excitation and loading of each port in a multiport data package (.mdp), and the results (scale factors, port voltages/currents/impedances, scaled far fields, near fields, currents) go to a .mcr file. The same executable archives data: it creates a .mdp from a manifest (.mdm) or expands one.
tools.usage: multiport_processor FILENAME.mcc [--scale-factors-only] [--combination name] [--quantities FarFields,NearFields,Currents] [--resultsfile name.mcr]   |   multiport_processor --create-package manifest.mdm   |   multiport_processor --expand-package pkg.mdp [dir]

parameters.name: --scale-factors-only
parameters.description: Only compute the scale-factor coefficients; no quantities are scaled.

parameters.name: --combination name
parameters.description: Process only one combination from the .mcc file.

parameters.name: --quantities
parameters.description: Quantities to scale; all if omitted.

parameters.name: --create-package / --expand-package
parameters.description: Archiver mode for .mdp packages.

tools.example: multiport_processor array.mcc --combination beam30 --quantities FarFields --resultsfile beam30.mcr
tools.notes: Syntax verified by running without arguments in 2026.1 (exit 99): the built-in help lists NearFields, FarFields and Currents, whereas the user guide page lists only FarFields as a quantity.

tools.name: envfeko and findinfostrings (environment and build diagnostics)
tools.description: envfeko (Altair Feko Environment Setup Application) prints the Feko environment exactly as the other components compute it at start-up - FEKO_HOME, FEKO_USER_HOME, FEKO_SHARED_HOME, FEKO_TMPDIR, FEKO_MPI_ROOT, FEKO_WHICH_MPI, I_MPI_ROOT, ALTAIR_LICENSE_PATH and PATH additions - in Windows batch format (default) or plain name=value form. findinfostrings prints the embedded build fields (APPNAME, APPINFO, VERSION, VERDATE, BLDDATE, VCSBRAN ...) of a Feko executable, or a single field. Both help when diagnosing MPI, licence, temp-folder or mixed-version problems.
tools.usage: envfeko [--winbat | --plain] [-d] [-v] [-h]   |   findinfostrings FILENAME [FIELDNAME]

parameters.name: envfeko --plain
parameters.description: Output as <variable>=<value> lines (default --winbat gives batch syntax).

parameters.name: envfeko -d
parameters.description: Additional debugging information.

parameters.name: findinfostrings FIELDNAME
parameters.description: Restrict output to one field such as VERSION; return code 0 if fields were found, 1 if not.

tools.example:
envfeko --plain | findstr /b "FEKO_ ALTAIR_"
findinfostrings "C:\Program Files\Altair\2026.1\feko\bin\runfeko.exe" VERSION
2026.1.0-8642
tools.notes: Not described in the 2026.1 user guide; behaviour verified locally by running 'envfeko --help', 'envfeko --plain' and 'findinfostrings --help' and on runfeko.exe/str2ascii.exe. Both are console tools that only read information.

tools.name: legacy_cfx_converter (pre-2022.1 CADFEKO models)
tools.description: Stand-alone converter that turns CADFEKO [LEGACY] models (.cfx created before version 2022.1) into the new CADFEKO format. The verbosity level controls how much conversion detail is printed, which helps to correct a legacy model when conversion fails; level 1 prints only errors and transfer categories and suits confidential models. Further options show which application versions created the file, convert the legacy media library or resave in the latest legacy format.
tools.usage: legacy_cfx_converter.exe FILENAME[.cfx] [--verbosity-level N] [--file-info[=xml]] [--media-library] [--resave] [--run-from-gui] [--version] [-h]

parameters.name: --verbosity-level N
parameters.description: 3: coordinates, labels and bounding boxes; 2: warnings, variables, geometry, entities; 1: errors and categories only; built-in help also allows 0 (no logging).

parameters.name: --file-info[=xml]
parameters.description: Versions of the applications that created and modified the file (flat list or XML).

parameters.name: --media-library
parameters.description: Convert the legacy media library.

parameters.name: --resave
parameters.description: Resave the legacy model in the latest legacy CADFEKO format.

tools.example: legacy_cfx_converter.exe model.cfx --verbosity-level 3 > output.txt
tools.notes: Verified by running with --help in 2026.1 (exit code 75) and in the CADFEKO user guide page 'Command Line Arguments for Converting CADFEKO [LEGACY] Models to New Format'.

tools.name: HyperMesh integration (.fhm Feko HyperMesh files)
tools.description: Feko exchanges meshes with Altair HyperMesh/HyperWorks through the Feko HyperMesh file (.fhm), which carries mesh elements, material properties and their assignment; CADFEKO imports and exports it as a mesh format and EDITFEKO reads it with the IN card (media from a .inc file with the same name). The user guide how-to 'Connect an Antenna to a HyperMesh Generated Mesh' places a 1 GHz CADFEKO patch antenna on a vehicle roof meshed in HyperMesh and remeshes the junction in HyperWorks so the meshes are connected.
tools.usage: HyperWorks: File > Export > Solver Deck (type Feko *.fhm) / File > Import > Solver Deck; CADFEKO: Home > File > Import (mesh .fhm), File > Export > Mesh (Feko HyperMesh, optional 'Scale to metre'); EDITFEKO: IN card 'Import Feko HyperMesh file'; Lua: ExportMeshFileFormatEnum.FekoHyperMesh

parameters.name: .fhm contents
parameters.description: Mesh elements, material properties and assignment data.

parameters.name: Mesh Boolean (HyperWorks)
parameters.description: Elements > Edit > Mesh Boolean, Union with 'Local remesh at contacts' creates mesh connectivity between antenna base and platform.

tools.example:
1) HyperWorks: export platform to vehicle.fhm
2) CADFEKO: import vehicle.fhm into the antenna model, unlink the antenna mesh, delete its geometry, Align it on the roof
3) export antenna + platform to .fhm, union and remesh in HyperWorks (Mesh Boolean, local remesh), export again
4) CADFEKO: import, Mesh > Replace > Replace With for antenna and platform meshes, solve
tools.notes: Verified in the 2026.1 user guide (how-to pages, CADFEKO mesh import/export format tables, IN card page, MeshImporter API). 2026.1 fixed PREFEKO error messages for .fhm imports to cite the correct .fhm line. Domain connectivity is the alternative when remeshing the junction is not wanted.

tools.name: Feko 2025, 2025.1 and 2026 new features
tools.description: Summary of the Feko highlights from the locally installed release notes for 2025, 2025.1 and 2026. Several items change defaults or remove components, so check them when older models, scripts or command lines behave differently.
tools.usage: Feko help > Release Notes (2025, 2025.1, 2025.1.1, 2026, 2026.0.1); PDF Altair_Feko_Release_Notes.pdf

parameters.description: Result-specific ground planes (several grounds in one simulation, applied in post-processing; not with RL-GO in 2025); any Z height for PEC/PMC/half-space grounds; multi-threaded volume meshing and aspect-ratio control for elongated triangles; multi-GPU MPI RL-GO and higher-order RL-GO ground interactions; multi-threaded PREFEKO; newFASANT removed from the standard installer.

Sinuous spiral antenna in the component library; FGMRES iterative solver (default for MLFMM and FEM/FEM-MLFMM); Domain-Level Preconditioner (DLP) for MLFMM; much faster plane-wave RL-GO; FEM distributed line port; PMC surfaces/regions in MoM and PMC FEM boundaries; more robust CMA tracking; PowerShell remote execution; Create Mesh with scope and optional proximity meshing; CUDA 12.8; newFASANT removed from the Launcher.

Faster MoM/MLFMM for large models; enhanced RL-GO for point sources and antennas; Reciprocal Excitation configuration (RT card, POSTFEKO Reciprocal Configuration macro); multilayer thick coatings on PEC; adaptive frequency sampling integrated into the solver (ADAPTFEKO deprecated); cable pin-linking, circuit duplication and path-from-wires tools; ODB++ media import; finite-thickness PEC/PMC layers in the planar Green's function; per-region automatic FEM element order; multi-GPU CMA; Windows-to-Linux PowerShell remote launch; LZ cards for all segment-port loads.
Patch releases; 2026.0.1 lists only WRAP changes; 2025.1.1 fixes regressions (e.g. wire port positions after transforms, a .cfm writing issue causing ERROR 2794).

tools.example: Upgrade check list: 1) scripts calling ADAPTFEKO -> use the solver's continuous frequency option; 2) MLFMM runs now default to FGMRES - compare iteration counts; 3) FEM runs pick element order per region since 2026 - re-verify mesh convergence.
tools.notes: Verified against the installed release-note pages 2025, 2025_1, 2025_1_1, 2026 and 2026_0_1 (help\feko\html\topics\feko\release_notes).

tools.name: Feko 2026.1 new features (AIS, run manager, optical coverage, HEEDS)
tools.description: Feko 2026.1 (installable as an upgrade to 2026 or stand-alone) adds the Advanced Iterative Solver, the RUNMGRFEKO run manager, an optical coverage tool and a Simcenter HEEDS interface, and changes CADFEKO save behaviour. The most important migration point is that CADFEKO Save now writes only the .cfx; solver input files (.cfm, .pre, .opt) are written when a solver component is launched or on Export > Solver input files (Ctrl+J).
tools.usage: Feko help > Release Notes > 2026.1

parameters.name: Solver
parameters.description: Advanced Iterative Solver (lower memory, robust parallel scaling, possibly longer runtime); interim results at relaxed convergence levels stored in the .bof (FP card); feko.mpi.exe replaces feko.csv.msmpi.exe / feko.csv.impi.exe; GPU direct sparse FEM (single node, multi-GPU); uniform RL-GO ray grid; automatic AMD AOCL maths library on AMD hardware; Touchstone export on early termination; multilayer thin dielectric sheets on SEP boundaries; PMC condition on FEM modal ports.

parameters.name: CADFEKO
parameters.description: Save writes only .cfx (scripts: add Project:WriteSolverInputFiles(cfxFileName)); CADFEKO_BATCH --force-mesh; optical coverage tool (line of sight on CAD geometry, no mesh); elongated-triangle meshing on by default; frequencies of interest for continuous ranges; simplified RL-GO fixed grid; legacy Parasolid Boolean option removed (region labels may differ); PCB import default materials; new library parts (elliptic/hyperbolic lenses, dome, conformal patches, dual-polarised patch).

parameters.name: EDITFEKO / POSTFEKO
parameters.description: CG card advanced iterative solver, FP card interim results, FR card frequencies of interest; POSTFEKO interim-result display.

parameters.name: Shared
parameters.description: RUNMGRFEKO for sweeps and model lists from CADFEKO/EDITFEKO/POSTFEKO; Qt 6.8.3; F1 context help links to the Siemens Support Center; Simcenter HEEDS interface to Feko.

tools.example:
-- 2026.1 CADFEKO Lua: Save no longer writes the .pre/.cfm
application = cf.Application.GetInstance()
project = application.Project
application:SaveAs([[C:\work\horn.cfx]])
project:WriteSolverInputFiles([[C:\work\horn.cfx]])
-- batch alternative: cadfeko_batch horn.cfx --force-mesh
tools.notes: Verified against the installed 2026.1 release notes (release_notes/2026_1). WriteSolverInputFiles(basename) is documented on the CADFEKO API Model object and used in the ParameterSweep example.
